title: Trump Administration Prepares Largest Mass Visa Revocation in U.S. History, Targeting Up to 200,000 Asylum Seekers
detail: The White House said August 24, 2026 that it is preparing to revoke as many as 200,000 B1/B2 (business and tourism) visas issued between 2016 and 2026 to foreigners who later applied for or are now seeking asylum — what officials called the largest mass visa revocation in U.S. history. State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said the department is 'coordinating with DHS to identify and revoke the nonimmigrant visas of foreigners who have come to the United States claiming to be short-term visitors, but then file for asylum to stay here permanently.' The move is separate from roughly 175,000 visas already revoked over the past 18 months for criminal convictions, accusations, or political speech. Revocation would not necessarily trigger immediate deportation, but would strip recipients of their status as short-term visitors while their asylum cases are pending, and is expected to draw immediate legal challenges.

title: Court Documents Reveal DHS Ran Far-Reaching Surveillance of Activists, Unions During Minnesota ICE Surge
detail: Court filings unsealed around August 24, 2026 showed DHS conducted extensive surveillance of protesters, labor unions, and community groups during the winter 2026 ICE 'Metro Surge' operation in Minneapolis-St. Paul, sweeping in a local teachers' union, a bicycle repair shop, and the Minnesota AFL-CIO. Documents describe an undercover DHS agent attending a February meeting of ICE protesters at Prince of Peace Lutheran Church, photographing attendees' license plates, and compiling dossiers with names, home addresses, and family and employment details. The government defended the tactics in a Friday court filing, saying it targeted only individuals later charged in a conspiracy case allegedly planning blockades at the Minneapolis federal building that served as ICE surge headquarters — not the broader body of peaceful protesters. Civil liberties advocates, including FIRE's Aaron Terr, said the methods described risk sweeping up people engaged in constitutionally protected activity.

title: ICE 'Operation Safe Community' Nets 1,328 Arrests Across Washington D.C. Suburbs in Virginia, Maryland
detail: DHS announced August 24, 2026 that a two-week ICE operation dubbed 'Operation Safe Community – Washington, D.C.,' conducted between August 1 and August 14 across Virginia and Maryland, resulted in 1,328 arrests, concentrated in the D.C. suburbs but extending into other parts of both states. DHS said roughly 400 of those arrested had been convicted of or charged with crimes including murder, attempted murder, rape, kidnapping, domestic violence, arson, and drug trafficking, and that members of MS-13, the 18th Street Gang, and Tren de Aragua were among those apprehended. ICE said officers proceeded despite sanctuary policies in many of the counties involved. Local outlets obtained video showing agents chasing, surrounding, and handcuffing people during the operation.
